3. At the instance of the certain interest persons the Settlement Officer of Dhaka initiated Misc. Case No. 2103/95 on 16.2.1995 and required the Assistant Settlement Officer, Dhaka to investigate after serving proper notice to the concern persons and to submit his report to him but it appears that without serving any notice on the plot owners of the society including the petitioners, although they are in possession by constructing their respective pucca buildings, submitted his report dated 25.4.1995 stating that the owners of the plots were not available at their given address. It is stated here that in the printed S.A. Khatian the name of Mrs. Gulshan Ali Hirji still exists as owner, in spite of the fact that the Society got its name mutated in the year 1984 in the records of rights with the office of circle officer, Tejgaon and paid rents to Mirpur Tahsil office and accordingly the said Assistant Settlement Officer issued notice upon the recorded owners Mrs. Gulshab Hirji at an old address where nobody lives in as much as she died in 1957 and for reasons, best known to the Assistant Settlement Officer, he did not serve any notice on the occupants of the plots in question, who are living there constructing their respective residential houses and that the said Assistant Settlement Officer, Dhaka, recommended for treating the said property as an abandoned property, which the Settlement Officer, Dhaka on 8.1.1997 in Misc. Case No. 2103/95 approved, treating the properties as abandoned property on the basis of the report of the Assistant Settlement Officer. The Settlement Officer prior to passing the order did not give any opportunity of hearing to the owners occupiers and that it appears that the Settlement Officer did not consult also the concern Revenue Office i.e. Office of the Circle Officer, Tejgaon, and that being aggrieved as such the petitioners made representation to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka on 24.1.1998 and/or 31.10.99 but without any result and that the property in reference has not been declared abandoned properties under P.O. 16.72 and also not published in the list of abandoned properties in the gazette notification under Ordinance 54/85 and that no notice has been served upon the occupiers till date for delivery of possession of the lands in reference declaring the same as abandoned property. It appears that on the basis of the order dated 8.1.1997 passed on an application filed by one Mrs. Sirin Begum and .50 others, the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Revenue, Dhaka, asked the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle to consider their application for Settlement of the lands in reference and said Assistant Commissioner (Land) has submitted a collusive report on 9.12.1997 but in the report it has been admitted that the petitioners are in possession of the lands, and now it appears that aforesaid Shirin Begum and others are instrumental in the initiation of Misc. Case No. 2103/95, and that having failed to get redress as aforesaid the petitioners caused service of legal notice on the respondents on 15.11.1999 through their lawyer. The management of the Society as vendors of the petitioners has also obtained a Rule in Writ Petition No. 3400/1998 on 3.11.1998 challenging the impugned decision and on which an order of stay has been granted. 

 4. The respondent Nos. 7, 8 and 9 being owners by purchase of plots in the lands in the same khatian got themselves added as respondents. The respondent Nos. 2-6 did not appear inspite of receipt of notice of the Rule in due course. The respondent No. 1 entered appearance by filing power but did not file any affidavit in opposition. 

 5. Mr. Salahuddin, the learned Advocate, appearing for Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury, Advocate on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the land in question admittedly be longed to Mrs. Gulshan Rdoshanally Hirji late wife of Mr. Roshanally Hirji, and said Mrs. Gulshan Roshanally Hirji died on 17.2.1957 and in support of the death the Petitioners filed Annexure-A and that the said Mrs. Gulshan Rowshanally Hirji left behind (1) Mr. Rowshan Ali Hirji as husband (2) Mr. Nasiruddin Hirji and (3) Mr. Boustan Hirji as sons and (4) Mrs. Najli Hasan, as daughter as her legal heirs to inherit her properties and all of them being members of the Shia Imami Ismaili community are Bangladeshi Citizens as has been confirmed by the government of Bangladesh and their property cannot be declared as abandoned properties in as much as they are present in Bangladesh although. The learned Advocate submits that there is no dispute as to the death of Mrs. Gulshan Hirji and about her legal heirs named above and therefore aforesaid legal heirs have inherited the properties of Mrs. Gulshan Rowshanally Hirji. After purchase of the land by the arifabad Co-operative Housing Society Ltd. an application for mutation of name in the records of right was made by the Society, which was allowed with due notice to all concern and the name of the Arifabad Co-operative Housing Society Ltd. was mutated on 13.3.1983 and copy of such mutated khatian has been annexed with the writ petition as Annexure-C and accordingly ground rents are being paid in the name of' the Society with the Tahsil Officer, Mirpur, copy of the rent payment receipts has been annexed as Annexure-C to the writ petition. The learned advocate submits that the treating of the case property as abandoned property by the settlement officer, Dhaka is illegal and without lawful authority in as much as he is not the prescribed authority to declare a property as an abandoned property under P.O. 16/72. The learned Advocate further submits that even in the list of abandoned properties published in the gazette under Ordinance 54/85 the case property has not been recorded and/or treated as abandoned property. The learned advocate also submitted that no notice has been ever served upon any of the purchasers occupants of the case lands, for delivery of possession treating the same as abandoned property and /or asked to explain their authority of possession as required under provisions of  P.O. 16/72 and Ordinance 54/85 and that as per decision of this Court no property can be declared as an abandoned property without serving notice as required under P.O. 16/72 or Ordinance 54/85. The learned Advocate also submitted as the properties have not been listed in the list of the abandoned properties published in the gazette notification Under the provisions of Ordinance. 54/85 the petitioners could not seek remedy in the Court of Settlement and that the petitioners have paid ground rents up to 1407 B.S. and as the authority has accepted the rents from the petitioners treating them as tenants under the government up to 1407 B.S. the impugned order of the Settlement Officer, Dhaka, declaring the case property as an abandoned property is not sustain-able in the eye of law.
